excluded.basis: TG18 cholangitis criteria (C2): group A met, but group B unmet (no jaundice — f.no-jaundice; total bilirubin 0.9 mg/dL, below the >= 2 mg/dL threshold; ALP and transaminases within reference, not > 1.5x ULN) and group C unmet (no biliary dilatation — f.us-no-biliary-dilatation; the stones shown are in the gallbladder, not the duct). Suspected cholangitis requires A plus one item in B or C, so the criteria cannot be met on this evidence. Charcot's triad is in any case insensitive (26.4% in the derivation cohort, C2), so its partial presence (fever + pain, no jaundice) never carried the weight the model learner gave it.

Revised Atlanta criteria (C5): 0 of 3 — the pain is right-upper-quadrant with scapular radiation, not the Atlanta description (epigastric, radiating to the back); lipase 92 U/L is within reference and far below 3x ULN (480 U/L); the pancreas was unremarkable on ultrasound. Two of three are required.

Excluded clinically, not by the numeric rule (its workbench posterior ends at 0.0201, just above the 0.02 rule-out line): pain is RUQ-localised with a positive Murphy sign rather than epigastric/ulcer-pattern; no peritonism (f.no-peritonism) argues against perforation; and a complete alternative explanation is imaged (f.us-positive). Residual uncertainty is recorded honestly: no erect chest imaging was obtained, so free air was never directly excluded.

Excluded clinically: no cough, dyspnoea or focal chest signs (f.chest-clear), and a complete alternative explanation is imaged. No chest imaging was obtained; the exclusion is clinical and is recorded as such.
Excluded by the safety-net pair: ECG without ischaemic changes (f.ecg-nonischemic) and high-sensitivity troponin below the assay's 99th-percentile upper reference limit (f.troponin-negative).

physiology_link.gap_statement: Design/07 specifies that the patient IS an engine state and that presented values are computed from the ground-truth perturbation. That specification is met here only at the baseline: the Milestone 8/18 engine models cardiovascular compensation (baroreflex, venomotor recruitment, transcapillary refill) and has NO inflammatory, febrile, or biliary perturbation — there is no engine state for acute cholecystitis, and this case does not pretend otherwise. The presentation's fever (38.4 C) and tachycardia (104/min) are authored case data, flagged as such on their findings; the engine's temperature variable does not exist and its heart rate at rest is 63.2/min, not 104. A biliary/inflammatory perturbation for the engine is named future work (Milestones 17/18 both record the missing biliary compartment).

presentation_stages.narrative: A 54-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with 8 hours of right upper quadrant pain that began about an hour after a fatty meal, is constant, and radiates to the right scapular region. The pain was followed by nausea and two episodes of vomiting. She reports one similar, milder episode three months ago that settled on its own. Vitals (case data): temperature 38.4 C, heart rate 104/min, blood pressure 128/78 mmHg, respiratory rate 16/min, SpO2 99% on room air. Examination (case data): RUQ tenderness with mild localised guarding; Murphy's sign positive; no palpable RUQ mass; sclerae anicteric; chest clear; abdomen otherwise soft with bowel sounds present. The learner must now commit a stage-1 differential board before any test result exists.
presentation_stages.title: History, vitals, examination

presentation_stages.narrative: Laboratory and bedside results return. The inflammatory markers are up (WBC 14.2 x10^9/L; CRP 86 mg/L). The cholestasis screen is negative: bilirubin 0.9 mg/dL, ALP and transaminases within reference. Lipase is 92 U/L — normal, and nowhere near three times the upper limit of normal. ECG shows sinus tachycardia without ischaemic changes; high-sensitivity troponin is below the assay's 99th-percentile limit. The learner re-ranks the board.
presentation_stages.title: Laboratory and bedside tests

presentation_stages.narrative: Right upper quadrant ultrasound: multiple gallstones (largest 11 mm); gallbladder wall 6 mm and reported thickened; a small amount of pericholecystic fluid; sonographic Murphy sign positive. The common bile duct measures 5 mm and is not dilated; no intrahepatic dilatation and no ductal stone. The pancreas is visualised and unremarkable. The learner re-ranks the board and commits a diagnosis.
presentation_stages.title: Imaging

presentation_stages.narrative: Adjudication and disposition. The case's adjudication block evaluates the TG18 criteria and severity grade mechanically from the staged evidence, lists what excludes each rival, and hands the patient to the Theatre for the operation the guideline recommends. The debrief (generated by tools/case_run.py, independently recomputed by tools/case_check.py) scores the attempt's boards against this adjudication.
presentation_stages.title: Adjudication, management, handoff

validity.consequences: Scores are formative feedback only; no credentialing, progression, or clinical decision may rest on them.
validity.internal_structure: Component scores derived from the case model by stated rules (cases/parameters.json); no composite score is computed, because design/07 defines components (Brier-style calibration, anchoring, evidence quality) and no weights — inventing weights would violate the precision law. Calibration proper needs a case series; one case yields per-stage Brier scores and board trajectories, and the debrief says so.
